newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Creditors to send inspectors to S.Korean Kia Group.
newsitem.headline: Creditors to send inspectors to S.Korean Kia Group.

text.p: Creditor banks were scheduled to send an inspection team on Monday to check on Kia Group's implementation of its self-rescue plan, a spokesman at the Korea First Bank said.

The five-member team from Korea First, state-funded Korea Development Bank and Shinhan Bank was expected to pay its first visit to the nation's eighth largest group at 0600 GMT. The inspections would continue until September 29.
Kia Group announced last month it would sell some 795 billion won worth of idle assets and cut the number of employees by about 14,800 by the end of this year.
Creditors put the Kia Group under bank protection until September 29 after they determined in July that some group affiliates were on the verge of defaulting on their debts.
"They will also inspect whether the Kia Group is settling its promissory notes smoothly for subcontractors," the spokesman said.
So far few of Kia's 5,000 subcontractors have defaulted but most are suffering from financial problems.
